Package com.hiface.sdk.capture

Interface FaceCaptureApi

public interface FaceCaptureApi
Face capture from images and live frames, obtained through HiFaceSdk.capture().

Interactive image requests share a serial queue with at most one running and four waiting requests. Further requests report BUSY through the callback. Use Blocking entries to process batch jobs one image at a time.

The SDK supplies the implementation; applications do not implement or construct this interface.

  • Method Details

    • facesFromBitmap

      @MainThread @NonNull FaceRequest facesFromBitmap(@NonNull android.graphics.Bitmap bitmap, @NonNull HiFaceResultCallback<java.util.List<FaceImageCapture>> callback)
      Detect once, align and extract up to ten faces, largest first. Empty list means no faces. Each result retains input pixel bounds and a capture or individual error (e.g. face smaller than 100 px). Uses the same snapshot, queue, cancellation and model lifecycle as fromBitmap; no liveness.

    • facesFromBitmapBlocking

      @WorkerThread @NonNull HiFaceResult<java.util.List<FaceImageCapture>> facesFromBitmapBlocking(@NonNull android.graphics.Bitmap bitmap)
      Blocking counterpart; do not modify/recycle the input until it returns.

    • fromBitmap

      @MainThread @NonNull FaceRequest fromBitmap(@NonNull android.graphics.Bitmap bitmap, @NonNull HiFaceResultCallback<FaceCaptureResult> callback)
      Asynchronously select the largest face in an image and return a feature and aligned preview. Face selection and size rules match extractFeature(Bitmap, HiFaceResultCallback).

      Use this method when displaying or saving the crop; the result includes approximately 433 KiB of RGBA data. Input pixels are copied before return, so the caller may then modify or recycle the original Bitmap. Image requests run serially, wait for required initialization, and load or reuse the feature model as needed. Results are dispatched asynchronously on the main thread. No callback is made after SDK closure or request cancellation.

    • fromBitmapBlocking

      @WorkerThread @NonNull HiFaceResult<FaceCaptureResult> fromBitmapBlocking(@NonNull android.graphics.Bitmap bitmap)
      Synchronous version for a controlled worker thread or batch job. Do not modify or recycle the Bitmap during the call. Returns both feature and aligned preview. For feature-only output, use extractFeatureBlocking(Bitmap).

    • extractFeature

      @MainThread @NonNull FaceRequest extractFeature(@NonNull android.graphics.Bitmap bitmap, @NonNull HiFaceResultCallback<java.lang.String> callback)
      Extract the largest face's feature from a Bitmap without a preview or liveness check. Use it for feature comparison, dynamic 1:1 referenceFeature, or face-library saveFeature/saveFeatures.

      No detected face returns IMAGE_NO_FACE. A largest-face width or height below 100 px returns IMAGE_FACE_TOO_SMALL; exactly 100 px is accepted. With multiple faces, select the largest by area. Dimensions refer to the input Bitmap pixels.

      The SDK copies pixels before returning, so the caller may then modify or recycle the original Bitmap. Requests run serially on the SDK image-processing queue, wait for initialization, and load or reuse the feature model as needed. Results are delivered asynchronously on the main thread. No callback is made after the SDK closes or the request is cancelled. Use this method for interactive pages and extractFeatureBlocking(Bitmap) for batch enrollment to avoid holding many Bitmap snapshots at once.

    • extractFeatureBlocking

      @WorkerThread @NonNull HiFaceResult<java.lang.String> extractFeatureBlocking(@NonNull android.graphics.Bitmap bitmap)
      Synchronously extract the largest face's feature on a worker thread, for sequential batch import. Use fromBitmapBlocking when an aligned image is also needed. Waits for initialization and model preparation automatically. Do not modify or recycle the input Bitmap until return.

    • startCameraCapture

      @NonNull FaceRequest startCameraCapture(@NonNull FaceCaptureListener listener)
      Start guided camera capture. FaceFlowStage reports no face, multiple faces, a distant face, an invalid angle, or an unstable face box. Follow progress and hold a steady frontal pose. On completion, the result contains an aligned preview and feature string from the same frame.

      All callbacks are dispatched asynchronously on the main thread. Page destruction that closes the SDK, SDK closure, or request cancellation suppresses callbacks not yet started. Lifecycle controls automatic closure, not the callback thread. Retain the handle only for early cancellation.
